Natural Language Query: Rank all the podcasts by their engagement i.e. total of impressions, shares and aggregate count of comments. List the id and name of the podcasts.
LLM Query:
WITH engagement_data AS ( 
    SELECT 
        e.podcast_id, 
        p.podcast_name, 
        e.shares, 
        e.impressions, 
        COUNT(e.comment) AS comment_count 
    FROM episodeengagement e 
    JOIN podcast p ON e.podcast_id = p.podcast_id 
    GROUP BY e.podcast_id, p.podcast_name, e.shares, e.impressions 
) 
SELECT 
    ed.podcast_id, 
    ed.podcast_name, 
    SUM(ed.shares + ed.impressions + ed.comment_count) AS total_engagement 
FROM engagement_data ed 
GROUP BY ed.podcast_id, ed.podcast_name 
ORDER BY total_engagement DESC;
Gold Query: WITH engagement_data AS ( SELECT e.podcast_id, p.podcast_name, e.shares, e.impressions, COUNT(e.comment) AS comment_count FROM episodeengagement e JOIN podcast p ON e.podcast_id = p.podcast_id GROUP BY e.podcast_id, p.podcast_name) SELECT ed.podcast_id, ed.podcast_name, SUM(ed.shares + ed.impressions + ed.comment_count) AS total_engagement FROM engagement_data ed GROUP BY ed.podcast_id, ed.podcast_name ORDER BY total_engagement DESC;

Natural Language Query: For each episode video, count the number of frames containing exactly one person, and the number of frames containing more than 1 person.
LLM Query:
WITH frame_counts AS ( 
    SELECT 
        f.video_name, 
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN o.type = 'person' THEN f.timestamp END) AS person_frames 
    FROM episodevideos_frames f 
    JOIN episodevideos_objects o ON f.timestamp = o.timestamp 
    GROUP BY f.video_name
), 
single_person_frames AS ( 
    SELECT 
        video_name, 
        COUNT(*) AS single_person_count 
    FROM frame_counts 
    WHERE person_frames = 1 
    GROUP BY video_name 
), 
multiple_person_frames AS ( 
    SELECT 
        video_name, 
        COUNT(*) AS multiple_person_count 
    FROM frame_counts 
    WHERE person_frames > 1 
    GROUP BY video_name 
) 
SELECT 
    spf.video_name, 
    spf.single_person_count, 
    mpf.multiple_person_count 
FROM single_person_frames spf 
JOIN multiple_person_frames mpf ON spf.video_name = mpf.video_name
Gold Query: WITH frames_with_person AS ( SELECT video_name, timestamp, COUNT(*) as person_count FROM episodevideos.objects WHERE type = 'person' GROUP BY video_name, timestamp ), frames_count AS ( SELECT video_name, COUNT(CASE WHEN person_count = 1 THEN 1 END) as one_person_count, COUNT(CASE WHEN person_count > 1 THEN 1 END) as more_than_one_person_count FROM frames_with_person GROUP BY video_name ) SELECT c.episode_title, fc.one_person_count, fc.more_than_one_person_count FROM frames_count fc JOIN episode c ON fc.video_name = c.video_name

Natural Language Query: Return the number of reactions per 10 sec interval for the video with the most reactions. For each interval, show the start time in seconds.
LLM Query:
WITH video_reactions AS ( 
    SELECT  
        video_name,  
        COUNT(reaction) AS reaction_count 
    FROM  
        episodeengagement 
    GROUP BY  
        video_name 
    LIMIT 1 
),  
reactions_per_interval AS ( 
    SELECT  
        video_name,  
        (engagement_timestamp / 10000) * 10 AS start_time,  
        COUNT(reaction) AS reaction_count 
    FROM  
        episodeengagement 
    WHERE  
        video_name = (SELECT video_name FROM video_reactions) 
    GROUP BY  
        video_name,  
        start_time 
) 
SELECT * FROM reactions_per_interval

),

Natural Language Query: Find the top 10 video frames ordered by engagement (total impressions) happening at the timestamp of the frame. Include video names, episode title, timestamp and total impression in the result.
LLM Query:

    SELECT  
        ef.video_name,  
        e.episode_title,  
        ef.timestamp,  
        SUM(ee.impressions) AS total_impressions 
    FROM episodeengagement ee 
    JOIN episodevideos_frames ef ON ee.engagement_timestamp = ef.timestamp 
    JOIN episode e ON ee.video_name = e.video_name 
    GROUP BY ef.video_name, e.episode_title, ef.timestamp 
)

    video_name,  
    episode_title,  
    timestamp,  
    total_impressions 
FROM engagement_frames 
ORDER BY total_impressions DESC 
LIMIT 10;

Additionally, provide the combined occurrence count for each object found across the top 2 episodes and the rest of the episodes. Each row should contain 2 columns, the count from the top 2 episodes and count from the rest.
LLM Query: WITH RankedEpisodes AS (SELECT episode_id, podcast_id, (impressions + shares) AS engagement_level FROM episodeengagement ORDER BY engagement_level DESC), TopEpisodes AS (SELECT episode_id FROM RankedEpisodes LIMIT 2), EpisodeObjects AS (SELECT eo.object_id, eo.video_id, eo.video_name, e.episode_id FROM episodevideos_objects eo INNER JOIN episode e ON eo.video_name = e.video_name) SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN eo.episode_id IN (SELECT episode_id FROM TopEpisodes) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS top_2_episodes_count, SUM(CASE WHEN eo.episode_id NOT IN (SELECT episode_id FROM TopEpisodes) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS rest_episodes_count FROM EpisodeObjects eo;
Gold Query: WITH RankedEpisodes AS (SELECT e.episode_id, e.video_name, SUM(ee.impressions + ee.shares) AS engagement_level FROM episode e JOIN episodeengagement ee ON e.episode_id = ee.episode_id GROUP BY e.episode_id, e.video_name ORDER BY engagement_level DESC), Top2Episodes AS (SELECT episode_id, video_name FROM RankedEpisodes LIMIT 2), ObjectCounts AS (SELECT CASE WHEN evo.video_name IN (SELECT video_name FROM Top2Episodes) THEN 'top_2' ELSE 'rest' END AS episode_group, COUNT(*) AS object_count FROM episodevideos_objects evo GROUP BY CASE WHEN evo.video_name IN (SELECT video_name FROM Top2Episodes) THEN 'top_2' ELSE 'rest' END) SELECT (SELECT object_count FROM ObjectCounts WHERE episode_group = 'top_2') AS top_2_count, (SELECT object_count FROM ObjectCounts WHERE episode_group = 'rest') AS rest_count;
